components.name: Measured Proof
components.description: Arabic composition bounded by the true text measure.
components.html: عَلَى قَدْرِ أَهْلِ العَزْمِ تَأْتِي العَزَائِمُ

narrative.overview: The interface behaves like a working type-foundry specimen: exact, spacious, and visibly concerned with measure. Arabic composition is the dominant visual evidence, while controls read as instruments around it rather than as generic application chrome. Cool paper, black ink, blue measuring marks, and a fine ruled grid make the page feel printed and computational at once. The system is dense where a typographer needs precision and quiet where the proof needs room.
keyCharacteristics: Arabic text is always the largest and most authoritative content in the workspace.
Ultramarine is reserved for active state, measurement, selection, and source-safe actions.
Hairlines and grid divisions organize the page without cards or shadows.
English utility copy is compact and technical; Arabic remains calligraphic and generous.
Controls use square geometry except where a circular thumb or pill track communicates movement.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Proof Blue is the only saturated color in normal operation; adding another accent weakens the measured state language.

rules.name: The Ink-on-Paper Rule
rules.body: Large regions remain cool neutral. Blue measures and activates; it does not become decorative atmosphere.

rules.name: The Proof Leads Rule
rules.body: English explains the instrument; Arabic demonstrates it and receives the greatest visual scale.

rules.name: The Mono Has a Job Rule
rules.body: Monospace is reserved for labels, values, status, and instructions tied to the typographic instrument.

rules.name: The No Floating Panel Rule
rules.body: Structure comes from shared edges and full-length rules, never from detached cards.

rules.name: The Printed Sheet Rule
rules.body: A component may change ink or surface color in response to state, but it never lifts off the page.

dos: Do give the Arabic proof enough space to be read before adding explanation.
Do align metadata, controls, and ruled boundaries to the shared sheet grid.
Do reserve Proof Blue for actions, measurement, focus, and active state.
Do preserve source-safe language wherever users might confuse a visual insertion with text mutation.
Do adapt the desktop split into a clear controls-then-proof sequence on phones.
donts: Don't add rounded cards, shadows, glass, gradients, or warm parchment effects.
Don't use decorative color where a hairline, scale change, or ink weight can carry hierarchy.
Don't reduce the Arabic proof to a preview thumbnail inside surrounding chrome.
Don't use monospace as display decoration or replace authored SVG controls with Unicode icon glyphs.
Don't introduce claims, metrics, or ornamental specimens that are not produced by the real tool.
